per_policy_guidance.guidance: Observed reliability: limited—5/12 (41.7%) in-distribution runs satisfied final red containment. Nine runs first met the containment predicate, but four of those no longer satisfied it at the final state; three never met it. Use is therefore not recommended as the default. Its red-anchored prior is intended for an observed, reachable red whose displacement dominates, but that benefit has no out-of-distribution validation. Avoid when the red pose is stale/noisy/unobservable, the red-to-buffer route is doubtful, contact/phase is ambiguous, or collision/recovery would be required. Recognize failure by lack of red co-motion after closing, red remaining elevated or following the TCP after opening, red outside or later leaving the center, premature blue disturbance, or material/persistent IK residual or limit contact; converged IK alone is not success proof. Handoff to place_blue only after direct observation that red is stationary in the supplied buffer and the gripper/TCP are open and clear; preserve both causal observations. If red is merely displaced but remains visible/reachable, a replan may refresh its anchor. If red is already settled, hand off rather than reacquire; unseen miss/drop/collision states require high-level reassessment.

Observed reliability: strongest and preferred default—12/12 in-distribution runs satisfied final red containment. All first met the containment predicate at steps 244–283 and were contained at the final state. Use for ordinary demonstrated geometry and for action-supervised intermediate approach, lift/carry, lower, release/retreat, or late overlap entries where TCP/phase uncertainty is the main issue. This support is limited to each training-segment entry and training call arguments; do not infer recovery or out-of-distribution robustness. Avoid gross red/buffer displacement, occupied or implausibly reachable buffers, collisions, misses/drops, or entries whose geometry matches no supervised phase. Recognize failure when the auxiliary phase conflicts with visible motion, closed fingers do not produce red co-motion, red stays elevated or follows after opening, or IK residual/limit contact is material; phase and finger closure are not contact proof. Handoff to place_blue on observed stable buffered red with open/clear fingers and TCP, not on the phase class alone; preserve both causal frames. A later handoff during visible blue closure/initial lift is action-supervised if red remains stable. If still in a recognizable supervised intermediate state, reinvocation can refresh the TCP-residual anchor; otherwise stop for high-level reassessment.

Observed reliability: none—0/12 in-distribution runs passed, and no run ever met the red-containment predicate. Do not select this policy for production runtime, including its intended moved-buffer/placement-dominant use: buffer relocation has no out-of-distribution result, and the policy failed even with the fixed training buffer and segment entries. Failure is red not reaching the supplied free region; also stop for red remaining elevated/following after opening, buffer occupancy, blue motion before red settles, or material IK residual/limit contact. If used only as an explicit unvalidated experiment, require a finite, free, plausibly reachable buffer and direct visual verification. Its documented handoff is to place_blue only after red is visibly stable at the actual supplied destination with open/clear fingers and TCP, while preserving both causal observations; later blue-lift handoff is described but not validated by a successful run here. Prefer buffer_red__h02 instead and request high-level replanning after a failed release or placement.

Observed reliability: partial—8/12 (66.7%) in-distribution runs satisfied final containment. All 12 first met the containment predicate at steps 238–297, but all four failures had lost it by the final state, so transient entry into the buffer is a critical warning rather than sufficient success. Use only as a secondary option when spatial displacement is the concern and visible causal geometry clearly identifies a supervised red-, buffer-, or blue-anchored phase; its displacement benefit is an unvalidated prior, not a measured result. Prefer buffer_red__h02 for ordinary geometry, ambiguous phase/contact, unexpected elevation/drop, or recovery. Avoid occupied/unreachable buffers and uncertain threshold states. Recognize failure by motion toward the wrong semantic anchor, red not following closure, red staying elevated after opening, red entering then leaving the buffer, premature motion toward blue, repeated gripper toggles, or persistent/material IK nonconvergence or limit contact. Follow the documented core handoff promptly once red is visibly settled in the supplied buffer and fingers/TCP are open and clear; do not require the optional blue overlap, and preserve both causal frames. A later handoff after visible blue acquisition/initial lift is supported only while red remains stable. If phase is ambiguous, stop or switch to buffer_red__h02 rather than treating h04 as recovery.

summary: Validation used each policy only from the entry state of its own training segment in the 12 demonstrations, with training call arguments, a 1.5× segment-length budget, and final-state red containment as the fixed exit rule. No out-of-distribution or recovery result exists. Runtime ranking is therefore: buffer_red__h02 as the default (12/12), buffer_red__h04 as a monitored secondary option (8/12), buffer_red__h01 as a weakly supported specialization rather than a default (5/12), and buffer_red__h03 disabled for production use (0/12). The intended displacement priors of h01/h03/h04 are design rationales only; validation does not establish those benefits. All policies require target_object="red", successor_object="blue", and a seven-value world buffer pose; validation used the training binding [-0.181, 0, 0.02, 1, 0, 0, 0], so changed buffers are unvalidated. For every policy, declare the skill complete from observation—not phase labels, gripper state, or IK alone—when red is visibly settled in the supplied buffer and the open gripper/TCP are clear, then hand off to place_blue while preserving the two causal observations. Optional overlap through blue closure/initial lift is documented, but no policy completed the full task in these skill-level tests and full-task success was not the scoring rule. On miss, drop, collision, occupied destination, wrong-anchor behavior, or geometry outside a supervised phase, stop and request high-level reassessment rather than continuing blindly.
